> for your help!

That was due to a bug in the installation scripts. Those scripts
assumed that you already had some packages installed, which you
didn't. I've fixed the script now, so it should not happen again.

Since you managed to install one package ('digest') before you got the
error, calling hbInstall() a 2nd time would probably install
everything without that error. Did you do that? From your other
messages on this list, it seems like you have succeeded in installing
the package, correct?

Cheers

messages.author: d8678873fd130940
messages.subject: Fwd: [aroma.affymetrix] failure in installation
parts:
Hi Henrik,

Thanks a lot for the help. I intended to install the package
on a server which is way more faster to handle the large
size data and came into that issue. I will re-do it again.
Meanwhile, I figured I should use R 2.6.02 and installed
it on my stand-alone pc. I succeeded and ran some sample
code by following the thread in the page:


http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis

I used almost exactly the same code for two cel files and got an error
message when I got to the script from the very beginning:

rs <- calculateResiduals(plm, verbose=verbose)

The error message was:

> rs <- calculateResiduals(plm, verbose=verbose)
Error in list("calculateResiduals(plm, verbose = verbose)" = <environment>,  :

I will attach the sessioninfo() and traceback() message at the very end.

So far I have 49 tumor samples and 138 normal samples. They are Affy SNP
250K arrays and not paired. Ideally, I would like to have the data analayzed
by aroma.affymetrix, such as normalization, estimated copy number (or
log2 transformed), and calling alteration regions. If you can shed some light
on this usage, that would be great.

Thank you very much and have a good evening!

Alex
